world.bio: Former ground staff at Jomo Kenyatta airport, laid off in the spring after seven years on check-in and gate duty. I know how a boarding pass is read at 4 a.m. and how to calm a passenger who has missed a connection. Now job-hunting, supporting my younger brother's school fees, and helping my mother with her poultry business on the side.
skills_assets: Seven years of check-in, gate and boarding experience at JKIA
Fluent English, Swahili and Kikuyu; a little French
Training in dangerous goods, passenger handling, and conflict de-escalation
A reference letter from my former shift supervisor
A smartphone, a small laptop and a patient neighbour who shares wifi
A mother's poultry farm of about 300 layers on the outskirts of Ruiru

projects.name: Gulf carrier assessment day
projects.text: I have an assessment day with a Gulf carrier in November. This is the third time I get this far with a Gulf airline; I failed the final-interview stage twice before and never got feedback. Each time I walked out knowing something went wrong and not knowing what. I practise answers in the mirror and record myself on my phone, but I do not know what I am missing.

projects.name: Mother's poultry business
projects.text: Helping Mama with egg deliveries on Saturdays. She has three hundred layers and a few regular buyers in Ruiru and Thika. I do the bookkeeping in a notebook and sometimes drive the delivery van. It pays little but it keeps me busy.

notes.text: Laid off in April, and it is September. Five months now. People ask, "have you found something?" in the voice you use for illness. I say "I am applying". They nod.

Church choir practice. We are working on a Swahili arrangement of "How Great Thou Art". The altos keep drifting flat. Our director said "the sopranos are the cause", and the sopranos looked innocent and offended at the same time. It was the first laugh I had this week.
Brother's school sent the fee reminder: term three, 18,500 shillings. I have 9,000 saved. Called my aunt; she said she would see. See is not a number.
Applied to four more jobs: two at ground handling companies, one cargo agent, one at a hotel front desk. The hotel one at least has a salary on the advert. Everything else says "competitive".
Watched a video on how to answer "tell me about a time you failed". I realise I have a lot of material. Not all of it is for interviews.
Mama's hens stopped laying for two days. She blamed the weather, I blamed the feed, we both blamed the cockerel. On the third day they laid sixty eggs. Chickens have no respect for our theories.

Spent two hours at the library and could not find anything about how assessment days at Gulf carriers actually work. All the blogs say "be yourself" and "smile". I smile all day and I have been rejected twice.

Brother Kevin has mocks in a month. He studies in the evening with a candle because the power goes off at 7. I sat next to him and asked chemistry questions out of his notes. I was surprised how much I remembered.

Final-interview stage: two years ago I lost on a role-play about a passenger who was angry about a delayed bag. I thought I handled it kindly. The interviewer had a face like a stone. No reason was ever given.
Choir sings at a wedding on Saturday. I get to wear the green dress. This feels like a small mercy.

messages.text: Kevin: Sis, they sent me home for fees. Me: When? Kevin: Yesterday. Me: I will sort it by Friday. Kevin: Sorry. Me: Do not be sorry. Study.
Grace: I will see what I can do for the school fees. Me: Thank you, Auntie. Grace: Have you found a job? Me: Not yet. Grace: Pray.
Brian: They are hiring at the cargo terminal. Me: Is it permanent? Brian: It is a contract. Me: I will apply.
Mama: The vet is coming tomorrow. Me: What is wrong? Mama: Nothing, I want him to look at the cockerel. Me: Mama.
Director: Rehearsal Thursday at 6, bring water. Me: Will do. Director: Do not be late. Me: I am never late. Director: You were late in August.

Egg delivery run with Mama, Thika, morning
Assessment day with Gulf carrier, Nairobi hotel, 8 a.m.

relations.about: Seventeen, in Form Four, wants to be an engineer
Poultry farmer, strong-willed, prays for my job daily
Helps with fees when she can
Former colleague, now at the cargo terminal

constraints: Needs income soon; fees due before Kevin's mock
Can only travel for interviews with at least a week's notice because of the family farm
sensitive: Two failed final interviews and no explanation weigh on her
The school fee gap is real and growing
